messages.text: Friday, November 6 · Canton, Michigan
Drizzle, Raga Jazz, and a New Dwarf Planet Candidate
Expect a damp and cool November day with a chance of drizzle. Tonight, catch a unique blend of Indian ragas and jazz, or explore mathematical concepts in Ann Arbor.
Today will be drizzly with a high near 51°F and a low around 39°F, carrying a 43% chance of precipitation.
Sunrise is at 7:14 AM and sunset at 5:21 PM, with a waning crescent moon 9.4% illuminated.
Local Flavors for a Friday

Experience "raga jazz" with pianist and composer Charu Suri at Cliff Bell's in Detroit at 7:30 PM. For a different kind of performance, the Go Comedy Improv Theater in Ferndale presents "Hip Prov" at 9:30 PM.
The Northern Taurids meteor shower is expected to peak on November 11.
Michigan Democrats Secure Legislative Trifecta
Michigan Democrats have regained full control of the state government, securing a legislative trifecta. Abdul El-Sayed won the U.S. Senate seat, becoming the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator.
Looking Toward the Weekend
Tomorrow offers an overcast sky with a high near 52°F. The Southern Taurids meteor shower peaked earlier this week, but the Orionids are still active.

Saturday, November 7 · Canton, Michigan
Quiet overcast skies and the weight of a historic Senate election

The day brings a steady, gray chill to Canton as the region processes the recent election of the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. Scientific inquiry meanwhile digs deep, linking Earth's mantle movements to long-lost geological history.
Expect an overcast day with a high of 46 degrees and a low of 34 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:15 AM and sets at 5:20 PM, with a waning crescent moon that is 4.3% illuminated.
Performances and benefit evenings

The Big Sky Company hosts a musical benefit for the ACLU at the North Star Lounge in Ann Arbor starting at 6 PM. Alternatively, you can attend a free performance of Jen Silverman's play Witch at the Keene Theater at 8 PM.
A community meeting is scheduled for the evening of November 11 at 6:30 PM.
Senate results and environmental policy shifts

Abdul El-Sayed has been elected to Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, marking a historic national milestone. In related policy news, Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is preparing to introduce a Data Center Bill of Rights to address infrastructure and environmental concerns.
